citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
The Program of Veterinary Care (PVC) does not indicate frequency of regularly scheduled visits to the premise and the
licensee states it has been a few years since the Attending Veterinarian has visited the site. The importance of setting and
conducting regularly scheduled visits by the veterinarian is to ensure that the animals are receiving proper medical care,
and that the veterinarian is familiar with the animals and facility in order to provide appropriate veterinary guidance. The
licensee must follow their PVC including having regularly scheduled veterinary visits to the premises.
Correct by 31 August 2026.

The contingency plan did not identify a chain of command. Absence of a chain of command and identifying who is
responsible for carrying out specific tasks required in emergency response may result in delays, confusion and/or poor
impact on animal welfare. Exhibitors shall develop and document contingency plans that identify a chain of command and
who (by name or by position title) will be responsible for fulfilling these tasks in addition to other items described in this
subpart.
Correct by 31 August 2026.

The facility has not conducted an annual review of their contingency plan. The last documented review occurred on 11
December 2024 according to the date modification timestamp on the electronic record. Reviewing the plan regularly
ensures the facility has made assessments for any needed changes to better prepare for emergencies. The facility shall
develop and document an appropriate contingency plan, as well as maintain review documentation and have it available
for APHIS inspections.
Correct by 31 August 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the licensee.
